text: I want to build a web app where my team pastes meeting notes and gets a list of action items with owner and due date. The team sees all open items on one board and ticks them off. It works when every action item from a meeting shows up with the right owner, and nobody has to retype them. Interview me in detail using the AskUserQuestion tool. Ask about technical implementation, UI/UX, edge cases, concerns, and tradeoffs. Don't ask obvious questions, dig into the hard parts I might not have considered. Keep interviewing until we've covered everything, then write a complete spec to SPEC.md.

I'll interview you in a few rounds and write `SPEC.md` once we've covered everything. I can't use the interactive question tool in this session, so the questions are below. You can answer in shorthand like "1b, 2a, 3: we use Slack names". Where I have a preference I've marked it **(rec)**.

## Round 1: Where extraction goes wrong

**1. How do you want to capture who's on the team?** Owner accuracy is your main success test, and it's the hardest part. Notes say things like "Sam", "SJ", "I'll take it", "we", "Design", or name a client who isn't on the team.
- a) Keep a team roster (name, nicknames/initials, email). Every owner must match someone on it, and anything that doesn't match gets flagged. **(rec)**
- b) Free-text owner names with no roster. Simpler, but then "Sam" and "Sam K." show up as two people on the board.
- c) Pull the roster from somewhere else (Google Workspace, Slack, etc.). If so, which one?

**2. When the notes say "I'll send the deck", who is "I"?**
- a) The person who pasted the notes
- b) Whoever the notes name as note-taker or facilitator
- c) Leave it unassigned and flag it for review
- Also: what happens with "we", "the team" or "someone"? Unassigned, or one item per person?

**3. What should happen when an item has more than one owner?** For example: "Priya and Tom to draft the proposal."
- a) Allow several owners on one item. Either of them can tick it off.
- b) Split it into one item per person.
- c) Require a single owner and flag it for review.

**4. When does an extracted item become official?**
- a) Paste, then a review screen where you edit, delete or add items, then publish to the board. **(rec)** The review step is how you meet "every item, right owner" without retyping: it's quicker to fix one field than to type a whole item.
- b) Items go straight onto the board, and people fix them there.
- If (a): can anyone publish, or only the person who pasted the notes?

**5. How cautious should extraction be?** Notes are full of maybes: "we should probably look into X", "Tom mentioned he might check Y", decisions that aren't tasks, and parking-lot items.
- a) Catch everything that could be a task, with one-click reject in review. **(rec, since missing an item is your failure case)**
- b) Only extract clear, explicit commitments.
- c) Extract everything but label each item as confident or uncertain.

**6. How should due dates be handled?**
- a) Relative dates ("Friday", "EOW", "next sprint", "before launch") should be worked out from the **meeting date**, not the paste date. Should the app ask for the meeting date, detect it in the notes, or default to today?
- b) If there's no due date: leave it blank, set a default (e.g. +7 days), or flag it?
- c) Is there a team calendar to use for vague dates like "next sprint" or "before launch"? Or should those keep their original wording with no date set?

**7. What do the notes you paste look like?**
- a) Short bullet notes typed by a person
- b) Full AI transcripts (Zoom, Otter, Granola, etc.)
- c) Both
- Also: roughly how long is a long one? A full transcript of a one-hour meeting is a very different extraction problem from 20 bullets.

**8. What should happen with repeats?** The same notes might be pasted twice, a corrected version might be pasted, or this week's notes might say "Sam still working on the vendor contract" when that's already an open item from last week.
- a) Detect likely duplicates of open items and suggest "link to existing item" in review. **(rec)**
- b) Only block exact duplicate pastes.
- c) Don't handle repeats for now.

**9. Where can the notes go?** This decides how the items are extracted.
- a) Sending notes to an LLM API (e.g. Claude) is fine. **(rec, since rules-based parsing won't reliably get owners right from messy notes)**
- b) Notes can go to an LLM only if it doesn't train on them or retain them.
- c) Notes must not leave your infrastructure, so it has to be a self-hosted model or rules only.

**10. Who uses the app, and how many are there?**
- a) Roughly how many people, and how many meetings a week?
- b) One team, or several teams with separate boards?
- c) How do people log in? Google or Microsoft single sign-on, magic link, or a shared link with no login?

Later rounds will cover the board and ticking items off (who can close whose items, undo, what happens to done items), notifications, editing after publish, linking each item back to its line in the notes, and hosting/stack.

Separately: several of your claude.ai connectors (Apify, Atlassian, Canva, Higgsfield, Notion, S&P Global) need to be authorized in your claude.ai connector settings before I can use them. That matters if you want this to pull notes from Notion, for example.

## Round 2

**11. Should the app use the speaker to work out who "I" is?** Transcripts label speakers ("Priya: I'll send the deck by Friday"), so in a transcript "I" is usually knowable. Your answer to 2 was to always flag "I".
- a) If the speaker label matches the roster, resolve "I" to that speaker and mark it confident. Without a speaker label, flag it as in 2c. **(rec)**
- b) Always flag "I", even with a speaker label.
- c) Treat a speaker-resolved "I" as uncertain: pre-fill the owner but mark it "needs review".
- Also: do your transcripts sometimes label speakers generically ("Speaker 2")? If so, should the review screen let you map "Speaker 2 → Marcus" once for the whole meeting?

**12. Must items be linked back to the text they came from?** Show each item with its source quote (e.g. "Tom: yeah I'll chase legal on the NDA") and a link to that spot in the stored notes.
- a) Yes, show the quote in review and on the board. **(rec)** This lets a reviewer check "right owner" in 2 seconds instead of rereading 15,000 words. The model must quote real text from the notes, and the app should check the quote actually appears there. That check helps guard against invented items.
- b) Only in review, not on the board.
- c) Don't need it.

**13. How do reviewers check nothing was missed?** Uncertain items are clearly visible. The harder failure is an item the model dropped entirely, and on a 15,000-word transcript nobody will notice.
- a) The review screen shows the full notes next to the items, highlights each item's source text, and lets you select any text and click "make action item". **(rec)** This gives you an easy way to check what wasn't highlighted.
- b) An "add item" button with a blank form is enough.
- c) Also run a second extraction pass whose only job is to find missed items (costs more and takes longer).

**14. What happens if two people review the same meeting, or someone walks away mid-review?**
- a) Save drafts automatically. Only one person can edit at a time, others can view, and there's a "take over" button.
- b) Last save wins, no locking.
- c) Don't worry about it. Unpublished drafts expire after N days.

**15. Can "needs review" items be published?**
- a) No. Every item needs a roster owner (or explicit "Unassigned") and a confirmed status before you can publish.
- b) Yes. They appear on the board with an "Unassigned" or "needs review" badge. **(rec)** Otherwise one unclear item blocks the other 14.
- c) Publish the confident items and leave uncertain ones in the draft.

**16. Who can do what on the board?**
- a) Can anyone tick off anyone's item, or only its owners? For example, Dana ticks Marcus's item because she saw it done.
- b) After publishing, can items be edited (owner, due date, text) and deleted, and by whom? Should changes be recorded (who changed what)?
- c) What happens to done items: hidden by default with a "show done" filter, archived after N days, or kept on the board?
- d) Is there any status besides open and done, like "blocked" or "won't do"? Or should v1 stay a plain checkbox? **(rec: open/done, plus a "dropped" state so cancelled items don't count as done)**

**17. What should the board look like?** With about 10 meetings a week, after a month you'll have 100+ open items.
- a) One list sorted by due date: overdue, then due this week, then later, then no date. Filter by owner and by meeting. A "My items" view is the default. **(rec)**
- b) Columns per person
- c) Grouped by meeting
- d) Should overdue items be highlighted? And what does "overdue" mean for vague-date items like "next sprint"? My suggestion: never overdue.

**18. Should anyone be notified outside the app?**
- a) No notifications in v1. The board is the only source of truth.
- b) Email the owners when items are published to them.
- c) A weekly or daily digest of open and overdue items, sent to email or Slack.
- d) Post to a Slack channel whenever a meeting is published.

**19. How do you manage the roster?**
- a) Who can add or remove people and nicknames? Is there an admin, or can everyone?
- b) When someone leaves, what happens to their open items: reassign them, flag them, or leave them?
- c) Should each roster member be tied to their Google account (email), so "My items" works automatically and ticking is attributed to them? **(rec: yes)**
- d) What if a nickname could mean two people? For example, if "Sam" or "T" matched more than one roster member, should that be flagged, the same way as an unknown name? **(rec: yes, flag, never guess)**

**20. How long do you keep things, given the notes are confidential?**
- a) Keep raw notes forever, delete them after N days (keeping only the items and quotes), or never store them (in which case source links break)?
- b) Should people be able to delete a meeting and everything extracted from it?
- c) Any data residency rules or approved vendors? For example, the Claude API with zero data retention, or it must run via AWS Bedrock or GCP Vertex under your existing company agreements.

**21. How should the app behave on the practical side?**
- a) Extracting from a 15,000-word transcript can take 30–90 seconds. Is it fine to show a progress state and let the user leave and come back to the draft? **(rec)**
- b) If extraction fails or times out, can the user retry? And should the paste be saved first, so nothing is lost? **(rec: always save the paste first)**
- c) Does the team work in one time zone? That matters for turning "Friday" into a date and for "overdue".
- d) Does the app need to work well on phones for ticking items off, or is desktop enough?

**22. Where will it run and who maintains it?**
- a) Any preference on stack or hosting? For example: "we're a TypeScript shop on Vercel", "must run in our GCP project", or "no preference, keep it simple".
- b) Who maintains it after launch: an engineer on the team, or should it need close to zero ops?
- c) What's your budget for LLM costs? At about 10 meetings a week, even long transcripts should come to a few dollars a month, so I'm assuming cost isn't a constraint unless you say otherwise.

## Round 3

**23. Which Claude model should extract the items, given the $20/month limit?** My estimate at about 43 meetings a month (10 a week), if every meeting were a 15,000-word transcript (about 20,000–27,000 tokens each), including the model's reasoning and output:

| Model | Price per million tokens (input / output) | Cost per long meeting | Cost per month, if every meeting is long |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Opus 5 (most accurate) | $5 / $25 | ~$0.35 | ~$15 |
| Claude Sonnet 5 | $2 / $10 | ~$0.13 | ~$6 |

Most meetings will be shorter, so real costs should be lower. Hosting takes about $5/month (see 24), which leaves $15 for the model.
- a) **Opus 5.** It gives the best owner and item accuracy, which is your main goal. It fits the budget in a typical month, but a heavy month could reach about $20. I'd set a hard monthly spending cap on the API account so the bill can't go over. If the cap is hit, extraction pauses until the next month and you add items by hand.
- b) **Sonnet 5.** Comfortably under budget, but somewhat more items will need fixing in review.
- c) **Start on Opus 5 and keep a one-line switch to Sonnet 5** if the bill runs high. This is what I'd recommend.

**24. Is this hosting setup OK, and who owns the accounts?** You want close to zero maintenance, a low bill and no engineer. My recommendation is **Cloudflare Workers on the $5/month paid plan**. The app, database, background extraction jobs and the nightly 30-day cleanup all run on one platform, with no servers to look after. Free tiers elsewhere have catches: some are licensed for non-commercial use only, and some databases pause when idle.

Whichever host you choose, someone at your company has to own three accounts and put a card on them:
- a) A Cloudflare account ($5/month)
- b) An Anthropic API account, which is where the spending cap from 23 is set
- c) A Google Cloud project to register the "Sign in with Google" app as internal to your Workspace. Some companies only let a Workspace admin do this.

Who will that be: you, or someone in IT? Also, is it fine for me to write a setup guide in plain language, click by click, as part of the spec? I'm assuming yes.

**25. Should anyone at the company be able to sign in, or only the 8 people on the roster?** Your company's Google domain probably includes people outside this team, and the notes are confidential.
- a) Only people on the roster can sign in. Anyone else in your domain sees "not on this team". Adding someone to the roster gives them access, and removing them takes it away immediately. **(rec)**
- b) Anyone with a company Google account can sign in.
- If (a): on first setup, the first person to sign in becomes the first roster member and adds the others. Does that work?

## Defaults I'll write into the spec unless you object

- **What the 30-day deletion means in practice:** after 30 days the full notes are gone. Each item keeps its quote, but "view in notes" links stop working and that meeting can't be re-extracted. An unpublished draft is deleted along with its notes at 30 days. It gets a warning banner from day 23 on.
- **Accuracy tracking:** the app quietly records how reviewers changed each draft: owners changed, items added by hand (these are items the model missed), and items rejected. It shows a simple monthly accuracy figure, so you can see whether the app meets your "every item, right owner" goal.
- **"Dropped" items:** a reason is optional. They're hidden with the done items.
- **Editing notes after extraction:** you can't edit the notes and re-run extraction on the same meeting. You'd delete it and paste again. Duplicate detection (a v1 nice-to-have) will catch the overlap.
- **Mid-review changes:** if someone edits the roster while a draft is open, the draft's owner matching doesn't update automatically. There's a "re-match owners" button instead.
- **Board updates:** the board refreshes when the page loads and every 30 seconds. It doesn't update instantly as others make changes, which isn't needed for 8 people.
- **Out of scope for v1:** notifications, calendar links, recurring meetings, time zones other than IST (all dates and "overdue" use IST), and a phone-specific layout. The board should still work on a phone.

I've written the spec to `SPEC.md`. It covers everything from the three rounds, plus the defaults you didn't object to. No application code was written.

**What the spec does to meet your three goals:**
- **Right owner:** the AI model only reports who the notes name, word for word. The app then matches that against the roster with fixed rules, including nicknames, accents, speaker labels and people who've left. Anything it can't match exactly becomes "Needs review" with a plain-English reason. It never guesses.
- **Nothing missed:** the AI is told to pull out anything that might be a task, including tentative ones. Each item's quote must actually appear in the notes, or it's flagged. On the review screen, anything the AI missed is still visible in the notes and one text selection turns it into an item.
- **No retyping:** reviewers only fix what's wrong. Items they don't touch count as accepted when they publish.

**Things to check before building:**
1. **Multiple owners.** Your round 1 answers conflicted: one said "one item per person if several names are given", the other said "several owners on one item". I followed the second, with a "Split" button for the first. It's easy to change (§16, note 1).
2. **Spending cap.** You asked for a cap but didn't give an amount, so I set the Anthropic limit at **$15/month**. With about $5 for hosting that keeps you at $20. If the cap is hit, the team can still review and add items by hand until the next month.
3. **Anthropic's data terms.** Your notes go to Anthropic's API. Check that its current data-retention terms meet your confidentiality needs; the spec lists this as your action item (§12).
4. **A test before launch (§15).** Hand-write the correct action items for 10 real past meetings. The launch bar is that at least 95% of real items show up, and no owner marked as confident is wrong. Re-run the same test if you ever switch to the cheaper Sonnet 5.

§14 is a click-by-click setup guide for the three accounts you'll own. My cost figures ($10–20/month in total) are estimates at today's prices, not measurements. The monthly Stats page will show the real numbers.
